subject: astronaut spacewalk
title: The 5 Longest Spacewalks Ever, Ranked (#1 Isn't American)

scenes.text: The longest spacewalk ever lasted over nine hours. NASA doesn't hold the record.
Number five: Sunita Williams and Akihiko Hoshide, 2012. Eight hours seventeen minutes outside the space station.
scenes.label: Williams & Hoshide · 8h 17m

scenes.text: Number four: two Chinese astronauts, May 2024. Eight hours twenty-three minutes outside the Tiangong station.
scenes.label: Shenzhou-18 crew · 8h 23m

scenes.text: Number three: three NASA astronauts in 1992, the first spacewalk with three people. Eight hours twenty-nine minutes.
scenes.label: STS-49 trio · 8h 29m

scenes.text: Number two: Jim Voss and Susan Helms, 2001. Eight hours fifty-six minutes, the record for 23 years.
scenes.label: Voss & Helms · 8h 56m

scenes.text: Number one: Cai Xuzhe and Song Lingdong of China, December 2024. Nine hours and six minutes in open space.
scenes.label: Cai & Song · 9h 06m

description:
The five longest single spacewalks ever: Williams and Hoshide (8 h 17 min, 2012), the Shenzhou-18 crew Ye Guangfu and Li Guangsu (8 h 23 min, May 2024), STS-49's Thuot, Hieb and Akers (8 h 29 min, 1992), Voss and Helms (8 h 56 min, 2001) and Shenzhou-19's Cai Xuzhe and Song Lingdong (9 h 06 min, December 2024).
Two later Chinese spacewalks (January and December 2025) are listed at about the same length as number five.
Could you spend nine hours in a spacesuit?
first_comment: Nine hours with no bathroom break. Which would you put at #1, and what should we rank next?
